name: toast
description: Accessible notifications: tree-scoped provider/hook plus an imperative toast() API rendered by <Toaster />.
designIntent: Toasts announce status changes without stealing focus. The provider/useToast pair covers tree-scoped usage; the module-level toast() + <Toaster /> covers event handlers and data layers where threading a hook is impossible (e.g. 1000+ call sites). A polite live region and auto-dismiss keep the queue quiet.

props.name: action
props.description: Single inline action; dismisses the toast after running.

props.name: duration
props.description: Auto-dismiss delay in ms; 0 keeps the toast until dismissed.

props.name: richColors
props.description: Tint the toast surface with its status color (Toaster component).

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the live region (Toaster component).

examples.title: Imperative API
examples.description: Fire from event handlers or data layers — no hook needed.

examples.title: Tree-scoped provider
examples.code:
<ToastProvider>
  <App />
</ToastProvider>;

const { toast, dismiss } = useToast();
toast({ title: 'Saved' });
examples.description: Existing provider/hook pair for component-scoped usage.

antiPatterns.title: Do not use toasts for critical errors
antiPatterns.explanation: Auto-dismissed messages can be missed. Render persistent inline error states (role=alert) for failures the user must resolve.

accessibility.implementation: Each toast renders role=status inside a labelled list; announcements never steal focus
Every toast has a labelled dismiss button (Dismiss <title>)

accessibility.userRequirements: Use duration 0 for errors that need a decision

guidelines: State what happened in past tense

compositionRules.relationship: Mount once near the app root next to your router; keep it outside transforms so fixed positioning is not affected
Use the provider/hook pair when the call site is inside the React tree
